hints: Focus on electrons first, water does not come from the ethanedioic acid half-equation, it comes from the manganate(VII) half-equation.
Five acid molecules each lose 2 electrons, so 10 electrons are lost in total and must be gained by $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions which each gain 5 electrons.
Recall that each $\text{MnO}_4^-$ reduced to $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ makes 4 water molecules, so work out how many $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions you need and then scale up the water.
walkthrough:
**Count the electrons lost by the acid**

Each $\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$ loses 2 electrons. For five molecules, the total loss is easy to find.

$$5 \times 2e^- = 10e^- \text{ lost}$$

**Write the reduction half-equation for manganate(VII)**

In dilute acid, purple $\text{MnO}_4^-$ is reduced to almost colourless $\text{Mn}^{2+}$. Oxygen ends up as water, so $\text{H}^+$ ions are needed to balance.

$$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Match electrons lost and gained**

We have 10 electrons lost, but each $\text{MnO}_4^-$ only gains 5 electrons. So we need two $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions.

$$10e^- \text{ lost} = 2 \times 5e^- \text{ gained}$$

**Scale up the water produced**

One $\text{MnO}_4^-$ makes 4 $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ molecules. Two $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions therefore make twice as many.

$$2 \times 4\text{H}_2\text{O} = 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

options.A: Not correct. 5 would mean one water per acid molecule. Water is not formed in the $\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$ to $\text{CO}_2$ half-equation, it is formed when $\text{MnO}_4^-$ is reduced, and the ratio is not 1:1.
options.B: Correct. Five acids lose 10 electrons in total. Since $\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$, 10 electrons require 2 $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions, giving $2 \times 4 = 8$ water molecules.
options.C: Not correct. 10 is the total number of electrons lost ($5 \times 2$) or the total number of $\text{CO}_2$ molecules ($5 \times 2$). It is a common trap to confuse electrons or $\text{CO}_2$ with water, but each $\text{MnO}_4^-$ makes 4 waters, not 5.
options.D: Not correct. 16 is the total number of $\text{H}^+$ ions used to reduce two $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ions ($2 \times 8$). Students often pick this by counting $\text{H}^+$ instead of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Remember $8\text{H}^+$ makes only $4\text{H}_2\text{O}$ per $\text{MnO}_4^-$.
